title: Geiger Counter Radioactive Sample Detection Lab
prompt:
Create a single HTML file implementing an interactive 3D Geiger counter radioactive sample detection laboratory using Three.js and GLTFLoader.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 5, 10) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (5, 10, 5) with intensity 0.8.
- Create a lab environment: a flat floor plane (20x20, gray material), a lab bench (box geometry 6x1x2 at y=1, dark brown), and walls (back wall and side walls using thin box geometries, light gray).
- Load the GLTF model 'facecap.glb' using GLTFLoader. Scale it to (0.3, 0.3, 0.3) and position it at (2, 1.5, 0) on the lab bench. This represents the 'detector apparatus housing' for the Geiger counter.
- Create a Geiger counter wand: a cylinder (radius 0.05, height 1.5, metallic gray) with a small sphere tip (radius 0.08, dark gray) attached to the loaded model. The wand should be a child of the facecap model.
- Create 5 radioactive samples as small glowing spheres (radius 0.15) placed in a sample rack on the bench at positions [(-2, 1.7, 0), (-1.5, 1.7, 0), (-1, 1.7, 0), (-0.5, 1.7, 0), (0, 1.7, 0)]. Each sample has a different radiation level: [10, 45, 120, 300, 750] counts per minute (CPM). Color them from green (low) to red (high) using a gradient.
- Create a sample rack: a box (3x0.2x0.5) at (-1, 1.55, 0) to hold the samples.

## Geiger Counter Mechanics
- The Geiger counter has a detection radius of 2.0 units from the wand tip.
- Radiation intensity follows inverse-square law: detected_CPM = sample_CPM / (distance^2), clamped to minimum 0.
- Total detected CPM is the sum of all sample contributions within range.
- The Geiger counter produces 'clicks': when active, generate random click events at a rate proportional to total CPM. Track cumulative click count.
- Background radiation is constant at 5 CPM.

## Radioactive Decay Simulation
- Each sample decays over time using the formula: current_CPM = initial_CPM * Math.pow(0.5, elapsed_seconds / halfLife).
- Half-lives for the 5 samples: [300, 120, 60, 30, 15] seconds respectively.
- Decay only progresses when the simulation is running (not paused).

## User Interactions
- Arrow keys (Left/Right) move the Geiger counter wand along the X-axis across the bench (range -3 to 3), step size 0.1 per keypress.
- Arrow keys (Up/Down) move the wand along the Z-axis (range -1.5 to 1.5), step size 0.1.
- Press 'G' to toggle the Geiger counter ON/OFF. When ON, the detector tip glows green. When OFF, it is dark gray.
- Press 'P' to pause/resume the decay simulation.
- Press 'R' to reset all samples to their initial CPM values and reset elapsed time to 0.
- Press 'S' to pick up / put down the currently nearest sample (within 0.5 units of wand tip). When picked up, the sample follows the wand. Press 'S' again to drop it at current position.
- Click DOM buttons: 'Shield Sample' button wraps the nearest sample in lead shielding (reduces its detected radiation by 90%). 'Unshield Sample' reverses this. Track shielding state per sample.
- Press 'U' for undo: reverts the last action (move, shield, unshield, pickup, drop). Maintain an undo stack of at least 20 actions.
- Press 'Y' for redo: re-applies the last undone action. Maintain a redo stack.

## HUD / DOM UI
- Top-left HUD panel showing: current detected CPM (updating in real-time), Geiger counter status (ON/OFF), simulation status (Running/Paused), elapsed simulation time in seconds.
- Top-right panel showing a table of all 5 samples: index, current CPM, shielded status (Yes/No), held status.
- Two buttons below the sample table: 'Shield Sample' (id='btn-shield') and 'Unshield Sample' (id='btn-unshield').
- Bottom-center: a radiation level bar (div-based) that fills proportionally to detected CPM (0-1000 range), colored green (<100), yellow (100-400), red (>400).
- An undo/redo indicator showing stack sizes.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- geigerOn: boolean
- simulationRunning: boolean
- elapsedTime: number (seconds, 2 decimal places)
- wandPosition: {x, y, z} (wand tip world position)
- samples: array of 5 objects each with {index, initialCPM, currentCPM, position: {x,y,z}, shielded: boolean, held: boolean, halfLife}
- detectedCPM: number (total CPM detected at wand, including background)
- totalClicks: number (cumulative clicks since counter turned on)
- heldSampleIndex: number or -1 if none held
- undoStackSize: number
- redoStackSize: number
- radiationBarLevel: number (0 to 1, fraction of bar filled)
- radiationBarColor: string ('green'|'yellow'|'red')
- modelLoaded: boolean (true when facecap.glb is loaded)
- backgroundCPM: number (always 5)
- detectionRadius: number (always 2.0)
physics_constraints: Radiation follows inverse-square law: detected = CPM / distance^2. Radioactive decay: current = initial * 0.5^(t/halfLife). Total detected CPM must be sum of all sample contributions plus background (5 CPM). Shielding reduces detected contribution by 90%. CPM values must never be negative or NaN. Conservation: resetting must restore exact initial CPM values. Decay is monotonically decreasing. Detection radius is 2.0 units.
